offence: Knowingly contravenes a protection order (family violence offence)
arrestable: May arrest without warrant — Women's Charter s.63D makes a family violence offence arrestable for the purposes of the CPC 2010 (overrides the under-3-years CPC default). Separate enforcement-officer power in s.64E (s.64E(2): entry if the officer reasonably believes the person is inside a place; check s.64E(1) on SSO for the trigger).
warrant: Summons (bailable under CPC default for imprisonment under 3 years; arrest column overridden by s.63D)
punishment: s.63C: fine not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment not exceeding 12 months or both; if aggravated under s.63C(2), fine not exceeding $10,000 or imprisonment not exceeding 18 months or both. Aggravated if the offence involves contravention of an order protecting a vulnerable adult and the offender has been convicted of another family violence offence involving contravention of the same order or another order that also protects a vulnerable adult.

offence: Offences relating to prostitution (sell/hire/procure etc. woman or girl for prostitution, carnal connection with girl below 16, etc.)
arrestable: May arrest without warrant — WC s.174(1): Director-General or authorised officer (police sergeant+, immigration officer, etc.) may arrest any person reasonably believed liable to prosecution for s.140(1) (and listed Part 11 offences). Overrides CPC term defaults. Not limited to in-view.
bailable: Not bailable (max 7/10 years — CPC default for other laws)
punishment: Imprisonment not exceeding 7 years and fine not exceeding $100,000; repeat offender: imprisonment not exceeding 10 years and fine not exceeding $150,000. Male repeat offender for certain paras also liable to caning.
